message.content:
{
  "question": "When should I see my doctor again?",
  "memories": [
    "azithromycin dose 250 mg",
    "acetaminophen dose 650 mg",
    "atorvastatin dose 10 mg",
    "aspirin dose 81 mg",
    "aspirin dose 81 mg",
    "Follow-up: Repeat chest x-ray, in 6 weeks"
  ],
  "original_lines": [
    "p1:L1 RIVERSIDE GENERAL HOSPITAL",
    "p1:L2 DISCHARGE SUMMARY",
    "p1:L3 Name: Angelyn Harris   DOB: 1965-11-10",
    "p1:L4 Admission date: 10/20/2026   Discharge date: 10/24/2026",
    "p1:L5 Diagnosis: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), right lower lobe. Type 2 DM.",
    "p1:L6 Hospital course: Treated with IV ceftriaxone and azithromycin. Afebrile x 48h, SpO2 96% on RA at discharge.",
    "p1:L7 Discharge medications:",
    "p1:L8 1. Azithromycin 250 mg PO daily x 3 more days (NEW)",
    "p1:L9 2. Acetaminophen 650 mg PO q6h PRN fever or pain, max 3,000 mg/day (NEW)",
    "p1:L10 3. Metformin ER 500 mg PO daily with dinner - continue",
    "p1:L11 4. Atorvastatin 10 mg PO qHS - continue",
    "p1:L12 5. Aspirin 81 mg PO daily - continue",
    "p1:L13 Activity: Rest, increase activity as tolerated. Use incentive spirometer 10x/hour while awake.",
    "p1:L14 Diet: Carb-consistent diabetic diet. Drink plenty of fluids.",
    "p1:L15 Follow up with PCP in 7-10 days. Repeat chest x-ray in 6 weeks.",
    "p1:L16 Call your doctor or 911 for:",
    "p1:L17 - Trouble breathing or lips turning blue",
    "p1:L18 - Fever over 101 F after 3 days on antibiotics",
    "p1:L19 - New confusion",
    "p1:L20 - Blood sugar over 300 twice in a row"
  ],
  "summary": [
    {"text": "You had a lung infection caught outside the hospital.", "sources": ["p1:L5", "term:CAP"]},
    {"text": "You also have diabetes (high blood sugar).", "sources": ["p1:L5", "term:DM"]},
    {"text": "Rest and slowly do more activity as you feel able.", "sources": ["p1:L13"]},
    {"text": "Use the breathing tool 10 times each hour while you are awake.", "sources": ["p1:L13"]},
    {"text": "Eat a diet that keeps your carbs steady for diabetes.", "sources": ["p1:L14"]},
    {"text": "Drink plenty of fluids.", "sources": ["p1:L14"]},
    {"text": "See your primary care doctor. Go in 7 to 10 days.", "sources": ["p1:L15"]},
    {"text": "Get a repeat chest x-ray. Go in 6 weeks. This checks your lung infection.", "sources": ["p1:L15"]},
    {"text": "Take Azithromycin 250 mg by mouth once each day for 3 more days. This is an antibiotic for bacterial infections.", "sources": ["p1:L8", "drug:azithromycin", "term:PO"]},
    {"text": "Take Acetaminophen 650 mg by mouth every 6 hours only when you need it for fever or pain. Do not take more than 3,000 mg in one day. This is a pain reliever and fever reducer.", "sources": ["p1:L9", "drug:acetaminophen", "term:PO", "term:q6h", "term:PRN"]},
    {"text": "Take Metformin ER 500 mg by mouth once each day with dinner. This is a diabetes medicine to help control blood sugar.", "sources": ["p1:L10", "drug:metformin", "term:PO"]},
    {"text": "Take Atorvastatin 10 mg by mouth every night at bedtime. This is a cholesterol medicine to lower heart attack and stroke risk.", "sources": ["p1:L11", "drug:atorvastatin", "term:PO", "term:QHS"]},
    {"text": "Take Aspirin 81 mg by mouth once each day. This is a low-dose medicine for heart protection.", "sources": ["p1:L12", "drug:aspirin", "term:PO"]},
    {"text": "Call your doctor or 911 if you have trouble breathing or your lips turn blue.", "sources": ["p1:L16", "p1:L17"]},
    {"text": "Call your doctor or 911 if you have a fever over 101 F after 3 days on antibiotics.", "sources": ["p1:L16", "p1:L18"]},
    {"text": "Call your doctor or 911 if you have new confusion.", "sources": ["p1:L16", "p1:L19"]},
    {"text": "Call your doctor or 911 if your blood sugar is over 300 twice in a row.", "sources": ["p1:L16", "p1:L20"]}
  ]
}
